patients.summary: Healthy construction worker who joins in 2024, then has a right open-globe injury and, weeks later, a ladder fall with left femur and pelvic fractures leading to disuse atrophy. In 2026 he develops sympathetic ophthalmia treated with prednisone and, after dental work in Thailand, acute hepatitis B that is resolving by today.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called asking to become a patient. Hasn't had a regular doctor in a few years. Works construction, asked for an early-morning slot. Booked new pt physical 8/20 at 7:40. Records release signed by e-form for his prior primary care office; request faxed today. Insurance card on file (PPO).

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o M here to establish care. No regular doctor for a few years. Feels well, no complaints today.

PMH: none. Only surgery was a laparoscopic gallbladder removal in 2021, recovered without problems. No hospitalizations otherwise.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: mother has hypothyroidism; father has high blood pressure. No autoimmune or liver disease in the family that he knows of.
SH: works construction. Single, lives in Chicopee. Smoked cigarettes, quit last fall and has stayed off them. No alcohol. No drugs.
Prevention: can't remember his last tetanus shot. No prior HIV or hep C testing that he knows of.

ROS: negative in detail.

Exam: vitals reviewed, normal. Well-appearing, muscular. HEENT normal, eyes with full EOM, PERRL. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. Ext no edema, full ROM. Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Skin clear.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance. Tdap today. CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HCV and HIV screens. Encouraged him to keep off cigarettes; congratulated him on nearly a year.
2. Hx cholecystectomy, no issues.

RTC yearly, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi August, your labs from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidneys, liver and sugar are all normal, cholesterol is in a healthy range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you, and see you next summer for your physical.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior PCP office (visits 2018 to 2022), 14 pages, scanned to media.

Summary for chart: seen for sports physicals and two sick visits (URI). Surgical referral 2021 with laparoscopic cholecystectomy that spring, uneventful. Problem list there otherwise blank. No medications. NKDA. Smoking documented as current at those visits. No immunization records included.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work for vaccines. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Influenza 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; updated COVID (Pfizer) 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Lots and VIS recorded. Waited 15 min, no issues, left for job site.

documents.title: Emergency department record (received 07/10/2025)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/08/2025.

28M with an injury to the right eye this afternoon, brought in with the eye shielded. Decreased vision OD and pain. No loss of consciousness, no other injuries reported. No PMH, no meds, NKDA. Tetanus: Tdap 08/2024 per patient.

Exam: well-appearing, vitals stable. Right eye with findings of an open globe; eye kept shielded, not manipulated further. Left eye normal, vision intact. No other facial injury.

Kept NPO, shield in place, treated per open-globe protocol. Ophthalmology consulted at bedside and took him to the OR this evening for primary repair. Admitted to ophthalmology overnight.

documents.title: Ophthalmology operative report (received 07/10/2025)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 07/08/2025
Preoperative diagnosis: open globe injury, right eye.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: primary repair of open globe, right eye, under general anesthesia.

The wound was explored and closed in standard fashion to a watertight seal. The globe was formed at the end of the case. No complications. Shield placed.

Discharged 07/09/2025 with a shield and our written post-op instructions; first post-op visit in our clinic later this week. We will follow him closely. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Post-ED check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after receiving the ED and operative records from 7/8. He saw the eye surgeon Friday, says the eye is sore but better, following the post-op instructions and wearing the shield at night. Out of work until ophthalmology clears him; he will get the work note from them since they are managing. No fever. Knows to call ophthalmology right away for worsening pain or vision. Physical next month still on the books.

events.reason: Fall from ladder with left femur and pelvic fractures

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (received 09/05/2025)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Trauma Surgery service.
Admitted 08/25/2025. Discharged 09/04/2025 to an inpatient rehabilitation facility.

Reason for admission: fall from a ladder with left femur fracture and pelvic fractures.

Hospital course: Arrived as a trauma activation, hemodynamically stable. Imaging showed the left femur and pelvic fractures; no intracranial, chest or abdominal injury. Taken to the OR 08/26/2025 by orthopedic trauma for open reduction and internal fixation of the left femur and the pelvis, uncomplicated. Postoperative course without complication. Pain controlled. Worked with PT/OT daily; limited by weight-bearing restrictions and pain, and needs further inpatient rehabilitation.

Other history: right eye open-globe repair 07/2025, followed by outside ophthalmology. Cholecystectomy 2021.
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: inpatient rehabilitation facility. Weight bearing per orthopedics. Orthopedic trauma clinic follow-up after rehab discharge. Primary care follow-up after rehab discharge.

events.reason: Persistent bilateral leg weakness after fracture fixation

documents.title: PM&R evaluation (received 10/09/2025)
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation, inpatient rehabilitation facility. Date of service 10/07/2025.

Reason for evaluation: both legs remain weak six weeks after fixation of left femur and pelvic fractures.

History: 28-year-old construction worker who fell from a ladder in late August, sustaining fractures of the left femur and pelvis, fixed operatively 08/26. Transferred here after his acute hospital stay. Mobility has been very limited since the injury. He and the therapy team note little gain in leg strength, so we were asked to look at the muscles. No prior neuromuscular disease, no systemic autoimmune disease.
Prior surgery: right eye open-globe repair 07/2025; ORIF left femur and pelvis 08/2025; cholecystectomy 2021.
Medications: none scheduled.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother hypothyroidism, father hypertension; no autoimmune or liver disease.
Social: former smoker, quit about two years ago. No alcohol. Construction work.

Exam: Awake, alert and cooperative. Vital signs stable. No fever or other sign of systemic infection. Lower extremities: very little voluntary movement in either leg, tone reduced bilaterally, patellar and Achilles reflexes hard to obtain. Upper extremities: full strength. Sensation intact in the upper body. Calves soft, no swelling or tenderness to suggest DVT; compartments soft, no sign of compartment syndrome. Surgical incisions healing.

Impression: disuse atrophy of the lower extremities after prolonged immobilization.

Plan: daily progressive strengthening and gait training here, advancing as orthopedics allows weight bearing; transition to outpatient PT at discharge. We will follow him in clinic after he goes home.

documents.title: Inpatient rehabilitation discharge summary (received 10/24/2025)
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Inpatient rehabilitation facility. Admitted 09/04/2025, discharged 10/23/2025 to home.

Diagnoses: disuse atrophy of the lower extremities; status post ORIF left femur and pelvic fractures (08/26/2025).

Course: Daily PT and OT. Leg strength improved gradually after the October PM&R evaluation. At discharge he transfers independently and walks household distances with a front-wheeled walker. Weight bearing as tolerated is pending orthopedic follow-up.

Medications at discharge: none scheduled.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: outpatient PT two to three times weekly (referral sent); orthopedic trauma clinic in 3 to 4 weeks; PM&R clinic in about 3 months; primary care within 1 to 2 weeks.

events.reason: Follow-up after hospital and rehabilitation discharge

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here after a rough few months. Seen once here last summer for a new pt physical; since then:
- 7/8 open-globe injury R eye, primary repair same day, followed by outside ophthalmology. Vision OD slowly coming back, he says.
- 8/25 fell from a ladder, L femur and pelvic fractures, ORIF 8/26. Acute stay to 9/4, then inpatient rehab to 10/23.
- PM&R at rehab on 10/7 found disuse atrophy of both legs (ED, op, discharge and PM&R records all reviewed).

Now home. Walks with a front-wheeled walker, slow on stairs. Started outpatient PT this week. Pain mild, no meds for it. No calf pain or swelling, no chest pain or shortness of breath. Eating fine. Mood: frustrated about being out of work, sleeping OK, no hopelessness. PHQ-9 4.

No meds. NKDA.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Weight 77 kg (84 a year ago). Comfortable sitting. R eye: no discharge, conjunctiva quiet. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Incisions L thigh and pelvis healed, no erythema. Calves soft, nontender, no edema. Visible thigh muscle wasting both sides. Moves both legs against gravity, weaker on the L. Upper ext strength full.

A/P:
1. Disuse atrophy after fracture fixation: improving. Continue outpatient PT; PM&R following.
2. L femur and pelvic fractures s/p ORIF: ortho follow-up 11/18 already booked.
3. R open-globe injury s/p repair: ophthalmology following.
4. Weight loss from the hospital stay, expect it back as he moves more.
5. Short-term disability paperwork completed today.
6. Flu and updated COVID today.

RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Orthopedic trauma clinic note (received 11/20/2025)
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopedic Trauma Clinic. Date of service 11/18/2025.

About 12 weeks after ORIF of a left femur fracture and pelvic fractures. Doing outpatient PT, walker. Pain improving.

Exam: incisions well healed. Neurovascularly intact distally on the left. Hip and knee range of motion improving.

X-rays of the left femur and pelvis today: interval healing of the fractures, hardware intact, no loosening or change in alignment.

Plan: advance to weight bearing as tolerated; PT to progress to cane as able. Return in about 3 months with repeat films.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up letter (received 12/11/2025)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology clinic. Date of service 12/09/2025.

Following Mr. Kearney after primary repair of an open-globe injury of the right eye on 07/08/2025. He has no pain and his right eye vision has steadily improved.

Visual acuity: right 20/40, left 20/20.
Right eye: wound well healed, anterior chamber quiet, no inflammation. Left eye: normal, quiet.
Intraocular pressures normal both eyes. Dilated exam unremarkable both eyes.

Assessment: recovering well after repair. We reviewed the signs that need a same-week visit, including any pain, redness or blurring in the left eye.
Plan: routine follow-up in 6 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: PM&R clinic follow-up (received 01/15/2026)
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
PM&R outpatient clinic. Date of service 01/13/2026.

Seen in follow-up for disuse atrophy of the legs after ORIF of left femur and pelvic fractures (08/2025). Home since 10/23, outpatient PT twice weekly. Now walking with a single-point cane in the community, walker put away before the holidays. Stairs one step at a time with the rail.

Exam: Strength: left hip flexion 4/5, left hip abduction 4/5, left knee extension 4+/5; right leg 5/5 throughout. Upper extremities full. Patellar and ankle reflexes present and symmetric. Sensation intact. Gait with cane steady, mild left Trendelenburg-type lurch without the cane. Calves soft.

Impression: disuse atrophy, improving well.
Plan: continue PT with a focus on hip abductor strengthening and gait without the cane. Return as needed; PT will send a discharge summary.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

documents.title: Orthopedic trauma clinic note (received 02/12/2026)
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopedic Trauma Clinic. Date of service 02/10/2026.

About 5.5 months out from ORIF left femur and pelvis. Walking with a cane outdoors, without it at home. No pain at rest.

Exam: incisions healed, no tenderness over the fracture sites. Hip and knee range of motion full. Distal neurovascular exam intact.

X-rays left femur and pelvis: fractures healed, hardware intact, alignment maintained.

Plan: no restrictions from our standpoint; continue PT for strength. Follow up as needed. Return-to-work timing to be decided with PT and his primary care physician.
Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Left eye pain and blurred vision

documents.title: Nurse triage: left eye
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called. For about two weeks the LEFT eye has been getting blurrier, it aches, and bright light bothers it. Thought it was eye strain at first. Right eye (the one that was repaired last summer) feels fine. No new injury to either eye.

Given his open-globe repair last July and ophthalmology's instructions to report any left eye symptoms, advised he call his ophthalmologist this morning and be seen this week, ED if vision drops suddenly or pain becomes severe. He called back at 9:30: ophthalmology is seeing him Thursday 2/26. PCP notified.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily with breakfast
Instill 1 drop in the left eye as directed, tapering per ophthalmology
Instill 1 drop in the left eye three times daily

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Lungs are clear. No hilar or mediastinal adenopathy. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Bones unremarkable.

documents.title: Ophthalmology consultation (received 03/02/2026)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology / uveitis clinic. Date of service 02/26/2026.

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Kearney, 29, urgently today for his left eye. Over two weeks his left eye vision has been falling off, with an aching pain and marked light sensitivity. His right eye was repaired after an open-globe injury in July of last year, about seven months ago, and has done well since. He is also still building back leg strength after last summer's femur and pelvic fractures.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none before today.

Exam:
Visual acuity: right 20/40, left 20/200.
Left eye, slit lamp: cells and flare in the anterior chamber, keratic precipitates on the endothelium, and posterior synechiae.
Left fundus: diffuse thickening of the choroid with several areas of serous retinal detachment.
Nothing to suggest infection in either eye. Intraocular pressure normal on both sides.

Workup today: ESR 25 mm/hr (mildly raised), CRP 10 mg/L (raised). ANA, rheumatoid factor and anti-double-stranded DNA all negative. Chest x-ray normal.

Impression: sympathetic ophthalmia, a granulomatous panuveitis in the left eye following the penetrating injury to the right.

Plan:
- Prednisone 60 mg by mouth every morning; we will taper according to response.
- Prednisolone acetate 1% to the left eye, frequent dosing to start, tapering as the anterior chamber settles.
- Cyclopentolate 1% to the left eye three times a day for comfort and to break the synechiae.
- I will see him again in 4 weeks, sooner if worse.
We would appreciate your help watching his blood pressure and blood sugar while he is on high-dose steroids.

Thank you for sharing his care.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u at ophthalmology's request. Dx sympathetic ophthalmia L eye 2/26 (consult letter reviewed), started on prednisone 60 mg daily plus prednisolone and cyclopentolate drops L eye. One week in. Says the L eye is already less painful, still blurry. Appetite way up, a bit wired at night, otherwise OK. No excess thirst or urination. No heartburn.

Legs: walking without the cane most of the time now, PT continuing. Ortho has released him.

Meds: prednisone 60 mg daily; prednisolone acetate 1% L eye per taper; cyclopentolate 1% L eye TID.
NKDA.

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP normal. Weight 80 kg (77 in Oct). L eye injected, pupil dilated from drops. Heart RRR, lungs clear. No edema. Gait without device, slight L limp.

A/P:
1. Sympathetic ophthalmia on high-dose prednisone: BP fine today. BMP for glucose and potassium, CBC. Counseled on steroid effects (appetite, sleep, mood, sugar). Taper per ophthalmology.
2. Disuse atrophy: improving, continue PT.
3. Not cleared for construction work yet, disability extended through next visit.

RTC after next ophthalmology visit or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi August, yesterday's labs look good. Your blood sugar, potassium and kidney numbers are normal, and blood counts are fine. We'll keep an eye on these while you're on prednisone. Let us know if you notice a lot of thirst or trips to the bathroom.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily with breakfast

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up (received 03/30/2026)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology / uveitis clinic. Date of service 03/26/2026.

Sympathetic ophthalmia, one month into treatment. Pain and photophobia much better.

Visual acuity: left 20/80 (was 20/200), right 20/40.
Left eye: fewer anterior chamber cells. Serous retinal detachments smaller. Pressures normal both eyes. Right eye quiet.

Plan: reduce prednisone to 40 mg daily. Continue prednisolone acetate on the taper schedule given today and cyclopentolate three times daily. Return in 4 to 5 weeks.

documents.title: Outpatient physical therapy discharge summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient physical therapy discharge summary. Episode 10/28/2025 to 04/16/2026.

Diagnosis: disuse atrophy of the lower extremities after ORIF left femur and pelvis.

Status at discharge: walks community distances without an assistive device, reciprocal stairs with rail. Strength: left hip 4+/5, remainder of both lower extremities 5/5. Single-leg stance improved on the left.

Plan: independent with home exercise program for hip strengthening. Discharged from skilled PT. Return-to-work clearance deferred to his physicians.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (20 mg) by mouth daily with breakfast

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up (received 04/30/2026)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology / uveitis clinic. Date of service 04/28/2026.

Sympathetic ophthalmia, two months of treatment. He has been away for two weeks and returned mid-April. No eye pain.

Visual acuity: left 20/40, right 20/40.
Left eye: anterior chamber quiet, synechiae broken. Serous retinal detachments have resolved. Pressures normal both eyes. Right eye quiet.

Plan: prednisone down to 20 mg daily, and we will hold there for a while to avoid a rebound. Stop cyclopentolate. Continue prednisolone acetate, now twice a day. Return in about 8 weeks, sooner with any change in vision.

documents.title: Disability form
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my disability company sent another form for you to fill out, I uploaded it here. PT discharged me and my legs are pretty much back but the eye doctor still has me on prednisone and doesn't want me on a site yet. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Disability form
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got it, August. I filled it out and faxed it back today, with work restrictions continued until ophthalmology clears you. A copy is in your documents. Good news about PT.

documents.title: Feeling sick
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Since about Sunday I've been really wiped out and kind of feverish, and I feel sick to my stomach. My pee has been really dark the last two days even though I'm drinking water. Eyes are fine. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: Feeling sick
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi August, the doctor wants to see you tomorrow morning. We booked you Wednesday 6/3 at 8:20. Please don't take any Tylenol or other over-the-counter medicines until you're seen. If you start vomiting and can't keep fluids down, notice yellow eyes or skin, or get confused, go to the ED.

results.test: Hepatitis B virus core IgM Ab

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 3 days of fatigue, feeling feverish, nausea without vomiting, and dark urine. Appetite poor. No abdominal pain unless he presses on the right side. No rash, no joint pain. Stools normal color. Eyes no worse.

New info today: he spent two weeks in Thailand, 3/30 to 4/13, and while there had a few teeth pulled and a root canal for a tooth infection. Didn't mention it before the trip. No other procedures, no tattoos. Denies alcohol, no Tylenol at all (and no overdose of anything), no supplements or herbal products. No known liver problems before.

Meds: prednisone 20 mg daily (ophtho taper); prednisolone acetate 1% L eye BID.
NKDA.

O: T 37.9 C. Other vitals reviewed, normal. Weight 77 kg (80 in March). Tired-appearing, not toxic. Conjunctivae: L eye mildly injected as at baseline. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness RUQ, no guarding, no rebound, healed lap port scars. No asterixis, alert and oriented. No edema.

A/P:
1. Fatigue, low-grade fever, nausea, dark urine with RUQ tenderness, 7 weeks after dental work abroad, on prednisone: concern for acute viral hepatitis. No gallbladder. CMP, CBC with diff, PT/INR, acute hepatitis serologies (HBsAg, HBc IgM, HAV IgM, HCV Ab). Fluids, no acetaminophen, no alcohol.
2. Sympathetic ophthalmia on prednisone 20 mg: no change for now, will update ophthalmology once labs are back.

Will call with results tomorrow. ED precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Results call: acute hepatitis B
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Labs from 6/3: AST 1680, ALT 2140, T bili 2.6. Alk phos and albumin normal. INR normal. CBC unremarkable. HBsAg reactive, HBc IgM reactive; HAV IgM and HCV Ab nonreactive. Picture is acute hepatitis B, most likely acquired with the dental work in Thailand in April.

Called pt and explained. Synthetic function is preserved (normal INR), so outpatient care is reasonable. Urgent GI referral placed; GI office reached, they will see him Monday 6/8. Reviewed: no alcohol, avoid acetaminophen until GI weighs in, no new supplements. Avoid sharing razors or toothbrushes; sexual partners and anyone in the household should be tested and vaccinated, and condoms until he clears. He says he lives alone. ED for vomiting, confusion, yellowing, or bleeding/bruising.

Messaged ophthalmology with the results re: his prednisone; they will coordinate with GI.
Lab will report to the state as required.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation (received 06/10/2026)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology & Hepatology. Date of service 06/08/2026.

Thank you for the urgent referral of Mr. Kearney, 29.

HPI: About a week of tiredness, low-grade fevers, nausea and dark urine. He came back from Southeast Asia in mid-April, where he had treatment for a dental infection, extractions and a root canal. No alcohol. No acetaminophen, overdose or otherwise. No previous liver disease. His history includes sympathetic ophthalmia diagnosed in February, on a prednisone taper (currently 20 mg), and disuse atrophy of the legs after last year's fractures, now largely recovered.

Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: no liver or autoimmune disease.

Exam: Mild tenderness in the right upper quadrant. Otherwise unremarkable abdomen, no hepatosplenomegaly appreciated. No stigmata of chronic liver disease. Alert, no asterixis.

Data: your labs from 06/03 show AST and ALT both above a thousand (1680 and 2140), total bilirubin mildly up at 2.6, normal INR, HBsAg positive with a positive core IgM. HBV DNA sent today.

Assessment: acute hepatitis B.

Plan:
- Liver biopsy this week to characterize the injury.
- No antiviral at this time: not a severe course, synthetic function intact. We will start one if the INR rises or bilirubin climbs.
- Hepatic panel and INR every two weeks, drawn at your office is fine; results to both of us.
- Prednisone: continue the ophthalmology taper; I have spoken with his ophthalmologist.
- No alcohol. Acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day if needed.
- Close contacts to be tested and vaccinated.
- We will see him in about 7 weeks. HBsAg, surface antibody and HBV DNA at 6 months from onset to confirm clearance.

reports.text:
Specimen: liver, percutaneous core needle biopsy, two cores, 1.8 and 1.5 cm.
Microscopic: hepatocyte ballooning degeneration with scattered Councilman (acidophil) bodies. No steatosis. Trichrome shows no fibrosis. Iron stain negative.
reports.conclusion: Liver, needle biopsy: hepatocellular ballooning degeneration and Councilman bodies, consistent with acute viral hepatitis in the setting of positive hepatitis B serology.

documents.title: Ultrasound-guided liver biopsy (received 06/12/2026)
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Interventional Radiology. Date of procedure 06/11/2026.
Indication: acute hepatitis B, tissue requested by gastroenterology.
Pre-procedure INR and platelets within normal limits.
Procedure: ultrasound-guided percutaneous biopsy of the right hepatic lobe via an intercostal approach under local anesthesia. Two 18-gauge cores obtained. Liver appearance on ultrasound otherwise unremarkable.
Complications: none. Observed 3 hours, vitals stable, discharged home.
Pathology to follow.

documents.title: Biopsy result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi August, the liver biopsy report came back today. It shows the kind of inflammation and liver cell injury we expect with an acute hepatitis infection, and no scarring. GI will go over it with you as well. Your next liver blood test is Monday 6/22, here.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Today's numbers are moving the right way: ALT 980 (from 2140), AST 610, bilirubin 2.1, clotting normal. Copy sent to GI. Next draw 7/6.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Another good step: ALT 340, AST 190, bilirubin 1.3, INR normal. See you Thursday.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u acute hep B. Much better: energy about 70%, nausea gone, urine normal color for two weeks, no fevers. Eating well. Biopsy (6/11) consistent with acute viral hepatitis, no fibrosis. LFTs falling: ALT 2140 -> 980 -> 340, bili 2.6 -> 1.3, INR normal throughout. HBV DNA 48,000 at GI 6/8. No antiviral per GI.

Eyes: L vision stable, no pain. Prednisone still 20 mg, prednisolone drops BID. Ophtho visit 7/21. GI 7/28.

Not drinking. No acetaminophen.

Meds: prednisone 20 mg daily; prednisolone acetate 1% L eye BID.

Exam: afebrile, vitals reviewed, normal. Weight 78. No RUQ tenderness today. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Walking normally.

A/P:
1. Acute hepatitis B, improving clinically and biochemically. Labs per GI schedule (next 7/27). Clearance check at 6 months per GI.
2. Sympathetic ophthalmia, on taper per ophthalmology.
3. Disuse atrophy, essentially recovered; home exercises.
4. Work: still restricted per ophthalmology; disability continues.
PHQ-2 1.
RTC September, flu shot then.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up (received 07/23/2026)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology / uveitis clinic. Date of service 07/21/2026.

Sympathetic ophthalmia. Since his last visit he has had acute hepatitis B, managed by gastroenterology; we have been in touch and agree with continuing a slow steroid taper.

Visual acuity: left 20/30, right 20/40.
Both eyes quiet, no anterior chamber cells. Fundi without serous detachment. Pressures normal.

Plan: prednisone to 10 mg daily, continue the slow taper from there over the coming months. Prednisolone acetate once daily to the left eye. Return in 6 to 8 weeks. Any redness, pain or blurring in either eye needs a prompt visit.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up (received 07/30/2026)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology & Hepatology. Date of service 07/28/2026.

Acute hepatitis B, about 8 weeks from onset. Feels nearly back to normal. No alcohol.

Biopsy 06/11: ballooning degeneration and Councilman bodies, consistent with acute viral hepatitis; no fibrosis.
Labs 07/27: ALT 110, AST 64, total bilirubin 0.9, INR normal. HBsAg still reactive. HBV DNA 310 IU/mL (48,000 in June).

Exam: abdomen soft, nontender today.

Assessment: acute hepatitis B, resolving as expected.
Plan: no antiviral. Hepatic panel in 3 weeks, then monthly until normal. HBsAg, hepatitis B surface antibody and HBV DNA in December, 6 months from onset; persistence of HBsAg then would mean chronic infection and a different conversation. Prednisone taper per ophthalmology is fine from our side. Follow up in December after those labs.
